C001.reason: The observation field `entity_id` must remain a string for v2 after the schema change to bytes. The decoded `entity.entityId` for v2 is now Uint8Array (bytes), requiring UTF-8 decode to string. v1 remains string (unaffected).

C002.reason: This line constructs a v1 Entity where `entityId` remains string per the unchanged v1 schema. The sample identifier "ts_303" is preserved as a string literal.

C003.reason: This line constructs a v2 Entity where `entity_id` changed from string to bytes. The sample identifier "ts_303" must be UTF-8 encoded to Uint8Array for the generated bindings. The observation pipeline will decode it back to string for the output key.

edits.before: const fields = { entity_id: entity.entityId, ...(version === "v1" ? { name: (entity as EntityV1).name } : {}) };
edits.after: const fields = { entity_id: version === "v2" ? new TextDecoder().decode(entity.entityId) : entity.entityId, ...(version === "v1" ? { name: (entity as EntityV1).name } : {}) };

rationale: Changed v2 entity_id from string to bytes per schema. For observations (C001), decode v2 bytes to UTF-8 string to keep output key entity_id as string; v1 unchanged. For sample construction (C003), encode the standalone identifier "ts_303" as UTF-8 bytes for v2 encode(); v1 sample (C002) remains string. All three subscribers independently decode both versions. No changes to tests, bindings, or v1 relay behavior.
assumptions: Generated TS bindings for v2 Entity.entity_id expose Uint8Array (bytes) for both decode output and encode input.
TextEncoder/TextDecoder are available in the Node.js runtime (global).
The sample identifier "ts_303" is valid UTF-8 and round-trips identically.
Arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes and mixed-version interoperability are out of scope.
Observation key 'entity_id' must be a string in JSON output for both versions.
